 CAN 2027: Central African Republic changes coach and recalls Kondogbia ahead of Benin
 Six days before their first duel against the Cheetahs, the Fauves have entrusted their team to Moroccan Abdelaziz Kerkache and called up 24 players, including Geoffrey Kondogbia and Louis Mafouta.

 Two meetings in Abidjan and Douala 
 Read In:
Français (Bénin) 
 The Central African Republic appointed Moroccan coach Abdelaziz Kerkache as head of its national team on Friday, November 6, just six days before its first match against Benin in the qualifiers for CAN 2027. The new coach subsequently presented a list of 24 players for the double confrontation in November.
 Geoffrey Kondogbia, midfielder for Olympique de Marseille, returns to the Fauves. Forward Louis Mafouta, who plays for Le Mans, is also among the recalled players. The two internationals are part of the main new additions to the squad selected to challenge the Guépards.
 Abdelaziz Kerkache arrived Friday morning in Bangui, where he was welcomed by the president of the Central African Football Federation, Célestin Yanindji. The Moroccan coach, who has notably worked with Mouloudia d’Oujda and several clubs in his country, succeeds Éloge Enza Yamissi.
 Two meetings in Abidjan and Douala
 Benin will host the Central African Republic on Thursday, November 12, at the Félix-Houphouët-Boigny Stadium in Abidjan, at 8 PM, Benin time. The return match is scheduled for Monday, November 16, at 5 PM in Benin, at the Japoma Stadium in Douala. The matches are part of the third and fourth matchdays of Group F.
 The Central African Republic approaches this double confrontation without any points after its defeats against Mauritania (3-1) and Burkina Faso (1-0). Benin has four points, like Burkina Faso, following its draw in Ouagadougou (1-1) and its victory against Mauritania (2-1).
 For his part, Gernot Rohr revealed a squad of 25 Cheetahs on October 31, highlighted by the first call-up of 16-year-old midfielder Parfait Faton and the absence of Steve Mounié, who is still recovering.
